pages.text: $(thing)QRP$() radios are low-power 20 and 40 m rigs in a wooden case: cheap (poor crystals work fine, they are designed around them), thrifty (2 FE/t, 13 transmitting) and gentle on nearby redstone.$(br2)The $(thing)HF receiver$() and $(thing)VHF receiver$() only listen.

pages.title: VHF Receiver
pages.text: An eight-channel $(thing)scanner$() for FM from 144 to 174 MHz: 2 m ham, marine and commercial VHF. Turn $(thing)VOLUME$() up to switch it on; all the way down clicks it off. Each channel has a slide switch under its red numeral: up is on.$(br2)Its own whip hears as far as a VHF handheld would from there; coax a VHF antenna to it for more (the whip is then cut out).

With two or more channels on it $(thing)scans$() them, stops on a signal and moves on a moment after it ends; the numeral of the channel it is on lights. $(thing)SQUELCH$() sets how strong a signal must be to stop it. $(thing)MAN$() holds it on a channel, $(thing)AUTO$() scans. A label over the panel shows the frequency; point at a switch for its channel's.

To change a channel's frequency, press $(thing)SET$() in and switch on only that channel: the SET lamp lights and $(thing)TUNE$() moves it, 2.5 kHz a click (shift 25 kHz, control 1 MHz).$(br2)It comes with 146.520, 146.940, 147.000, marine 16 and 9, 154.280, 155.475 and the 162.550 weather channel.

It runs from a power wire, or from a $(item)Small NiCd$() or $(item)Small Alkaline Battery$(): shift + right-click it with the cell, with an empty hand to take it out.$(br2)On the cell alone it listens about ten days, half as long as a weather alert receiver, and far less while it plays signals. The wire never charges the cell, and a flat alkaline comes out dead.
